Jimenez reckless driving case postponed

July 20, 2026
#courts, #Jimenez, #traffic
15
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:26
Instaread

The reckless driving charge against Mason Supervisor Andres Jimenez has been continued to Sept. 21.

Jimenez was charged with driving 104 mph in a 70 mph zone, which is considered reckless driving under state law. According to the Virginia State Police, he was driving a 2025 Porsche on the Route 66 express lanes shortly before 9 a.m. on May 5.

Jimenez was scheduled to appear in Traffic Court on July 20. The Fairfax County Commonwealth’s Attorney asked to be recused from the case, so Judge Darwyn Easley on July 20 in Traffic Court granted a request by Jimenez’s attorney, Makan Shirafkan, to continue the case. Jimenez did not appear in court.

Related story: Jimenez charged with driving 104 mph in Fairfax

Jimenez and Commonwealth’s Attorney Steve Descano have close political ties, and as a member of the Board of Supervisors, Jimenez oversees the Commonwealth’s Attorney’s budget.

The Commonwealth Attorney’s office issued the following statement: “Fairfax community members trust our office to prosecute cases fairly and hold individuals accountable when they break the law, regardless of their identity. We highly value this trust and would not want to give even the slightest appearance otherwise. We will therefore request that the court appoint a special prosecutor from another jurisdiction to handle the pending case against Fairfax County Supervisor Andres Jimenez.”

A General District Court judge will appoint a prosecutor from a nearby jurisdiction, possibly as early as this week.
